Standard: Design criteria derive from the intended operational usage and comprehensively address AW for the mission usage, full permissible flight envelope, duty cycle, interfaces, induced and natural environment, inspection capability, and maintenance philosophy. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) The CONOPS/OMS/MP establishes the intended operational usage. This includes the intended mission usage, flight envelope, maintenance philosophy, and the tasks, events, durations, frequencies, and environments associated with air system operations.
(2) For UAS, the intended operational usage includes expectations for levels of air system autonomy, C2 requirements, and intended usage of the FTS. It also addresses any special military modes requiring functional and physical separation from SCFs.
(3) Systems engineering planning documentation addresses definition of the functional and allocated baselines for translation into the system architecture hierarchy. It also describes the planned activities, including technical reviews and audits, to show verification to the specification requirements and validation of the operational requirements.
(4) For air systems reliant upon DoW Component AW authority-accepted design approvals (e.g., FAA type design approval for CDA), systems engineering planning and specification documentation accounts for variations and deviations in operational usage. At the discretion of the issuing authority, the variations and deviations do not invalidate the underlying design approval.
(5) The specification requirements translate operational needs into a set of a technical requirements and comprehensively define safety-critical functionality at the system level. Allocation of specification requirements associated with SCFs and sub-functions occurs throughout the system architecture hierarchy and addresses the intended function of the physical architecture, including hardware, software, and crewmember actions. This requirements allocation and traceability shows comprehensive materiel solution alignment to the entirety of the intended operational usage.
(6) The TEMP, flight test plans, and flight test procedures include verification activities that align with the intended operational usage and confirm the air system functions as intended. The scope of testing addresses the requirements that need flight test to complete verification. The TEMP identifies the resources to execute a production-relevant test to support validation of operational usage of the air system.
(7) Systems engineering planning documentation describes a closed-loop process for addressing deficiency and problem reports identified during verification activities and ensures traceability for deficiency and problem reports that impact SCFs. Evidence for process adherence demonstrates clear identification, analysis, and resolution of issues with record of planned or completed changes to design, specification requirements, verification activities, and mitigations. Deficiency and problem reports associated with SCFs are corrected or mitigated.
(8) Verification of SCFs indicates readiness to enter flight test. Evidence from completed verification activities supports execution to intended operational usage and positioning for AW approval to begin flight test.
(9) Validation or accreditation and acceptance of models and simulations used to verify SCFs ensures the intended usage aligns with the air system’s operational usage. This includes verification of analysis tools (e.g., FEA) that are inputs to the model or simulation. When documenting this validation or accreditation, include the intended use, modeling and simulation requirements and acceptability criteria, assumptions, capabilities, limitations, risks, impacts, and V&V or accreditation agent IAW MIL-STD-3022, V&V Report Template appendix or Accreditation Report Template appendix. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Examination.
(10) Evidence of a closed-loop process for addressing deficiency and problem reports associated with SCFs shows completion of changes to design, specification requirements, verification activities, and mitigations documented in USG verified technical data. Deficiencies associated with SCFs are corrected or mitigated.
(11) Verification of SCFs, using a production-representative article, shows air system AW for the intended operational usage. Evidence from completed verification activities supports validation of production-representative articles to the intended operational usage and entry into operations.
